raw_recipe.headline: Ham and Cheese Breakfast Casserole
raw_recipe.description: A hearty ham and cheese breakfast casserole with a crispy cornflake topping.
raw_recipe.name: Ham and Cheese Breakfast Casserole

review.reviewBody: Try substituting crushed canned onion rings for the corn flakes. I eliminated the onion powder and did this. I also reduced the cheddar chees by 1/2 cup. It was fabulous and everyone took the recipe home!

I love this recipe! It's so simple and you can make it the night before for brunch or breakfast. After making it a few times I only made a few minor changes. I used 16 slices of bread, deli sliced ham, and sliced cheese instead of shredded. I used 8 eggs, 3 cups of milk, 1/2 teaspoon mustard powder, 2 teaspoons of salt and 1/4 teaspoon of pepper. I increased the cornflakes to 5 cups (crushed well) and 1/2 cup of melted margarine. I then layered in the following order bread, ham, cheese, ham, cheese, bread. I found that if you layer the ham and cheese it’s more evenly distributed. I poured the egg mixture over, then cornflakes and baked at 350 for one hour. Awesome!

Put this together last night for breakfast this morning. I halved it since there are only two of us tho I did add an extra egg (totaling 4). I made it as is except I toasted the bread cubes (I had white burger buns & they worked fine!) & added chopped chives since I got my recipes mixed up & bought them mistakenly, so I added them. We weren’t crazy about the topping due to the bit of sweetness, I would use regular breadcrumbs or maybe try someone’s suggestion of French fried onions instead. Cheese & ham mix was very tasty. I will make this again & may experiment with sautéed onions and peppers in the mix.

Has become a favorite, but I made a few changes. Substituted bread with 1 1/2 pkg. frozen o'brien potatoes, used 8 eggs instead of 6, and instead of 3 1/2 c. of milk, I used 3 c. milk & 1/2 cup of half n half. Also added 1/2 cup diced green onions, plus added another 1/2 c. of ham. Baked for about 50-55 minutes. Has been requested by family & friends for various brunches & holiday functions. Have given recipe to at least 12 people in last 3 years! Usually only a small amount is left after a meal.

I thought this was pretty yummy! I made it for Chrismas Breakfast. I only made a couple of changes; I used frozen shredded potatoes instead of bread and I used French's Fried Onions instead of Cornflakes. Oh, and I also added a couple extra eggs and a layer of chopped sweet onion! It took about an hour and a half to cook all the way. I put it in before we started opening the gifts and it was finished when we were done opening. Next time, instead of just diced ham, I would use sliced ham and then dice it, just for a better texture. Overall though this was quite good and everyone loved it! It's also great with a little cholula sauce!

I gave this recip 5 stars after some tweaking. I used only 1 1/2 cups of cheddar cheese. I put 1 cup of it into the mix, and omited the cornflakes and added the other 1/2 cup on top of the finished casserole just prior to baking. I also reduced the swiss cheese to 1 cup. I made the casserole with 10 eggs. I also added 1/2 a cup of broccoli florets, 1/2 a cup of diced onions instead of onion powder, and a little bit of leftover green and red peppers. I used potato bread instead of white and tore it up into small chunks and placed in the bottom of the pan. I made this over Christmas when we had several relatives spending the night. I was hoping for leftovers but it was all gobbled up and people took home the recipe!

Great dish! Instead of using breAd crumbs,however, I like to use hashbrowns. The frozen bag with the onions and peppers already in it is the way to go. All I do is brown them on the stove before Mixing them with the rest of the ingredients to bake. While they are browning, I like to spice them up with salt,pepper, ground mustard,onion powered and a touch of hot sauce. Add the hashbrowns to the dish first then pour your eggs on top. Then add whatever meat you'd like and top with cheese! Works out a little better than bread because it's not so soft..it's more of a hearty breakfast taste with more flavor!

This is a good recipe. I use leftover ham from a ham I cooked in the crockpot. I changed one thing. Rather than using bread I used a bag of hash browns, the kind that is in the refrigerated section of the market. Other than that I made no changes and it tasted great. I like to cut this up and freeze it in single serving sizes, thaw it out in the fridge the night before and then pop into the microwave to heat the next morning. Makes a quick and filling breakfast and cheaper than fast food. A little salsa served alongside is a great addition.

Score... I've been looking for this recipe! My mom used to make it every Christmas morning. She used potato chips instead of corn flakes, and added fresh diced onions, mushrooms, and green peppers, but other than that, this is it.

As a FACS teacher, I have used this with students for a number of years. It has always been a great hit, numerous requests for recipe. I've used various cereals (what was left in pantry at end of school year. (Corn flakes, a Rice Krispies, Chex, etc). I've substituted whole wheat for half of bread. Changed cheeses - not all kids are big on Swiss. (Monterey Jack, Pepper Jack, etc)
Tried rye for 1/4 of bread... Too strong, maybe 2-3 slices.

This has been a very popular recipe whenever I've made it, whether for family or for groups, and making it the night before just makes it so stress-free. I use 15 bread slices and 7 eggs, and it truly doesn't need more than 1/4 cup of melted butter. It's delicious!!
I subbed gruyere cheese for the Swiss and added a small amount of diced sweet red bell pepper to the eggs for color and then followed the rest of the recipe. Everyone loved it!
This is such a yummy casserole! The cornflakes added a crunch. Definitely making this again.
Made it for our family Christmas morning. everyone loved it

I made this and the Overnight Blueberry French Toast for a brunch, and although everybody raved about both, there wasn't any of this one left! I added some frozen O'Brien Potatoes with peppers and onions in with the ham and cheeses. Definately will be making this one again!
I added garlic powder as someone suggested, the seasoning was right. Will add more ham, less bread next time I make it. Good use of leftover easter ham!

I like this type of dish for weekends/holidays when we have guests because it saves me from being a "short order cook" every morning. I used a bit less milk and butter, and found it needed a bit more cooking, but overall it was well received and we had some leftovers which were very good reheated.
I added an extra egg and would use approximately 10-12 ounces of bread. A little to much bread for me no per my family. Good flavor.
This was a big hit with my family for Christmas brunch! My son in law had thirds! Easy to make- great flavor with the 2 cheeses!

I made it for Christmas the last two years. I added two more eggs, onions and green peppers and a touch of pepper. It was a huge hit! I'm actually looking at it again because my wife wants me to make it for a women's church event!
